conventions.decision: AI full-text eligibility recommendation, distinct from final human/formal inclusion.
conventions.read_extent: Eligibility requires sufficient full-text evidence for every criterion, not independent verification of every proof, appendix or codebase. Inspected extent and version are specified per record.
conventions.features: Only feature_codes fields are verified in this checkpoint. Other legacy feature codes remain provisional. No means not demonstrated in the inspected evidence/version; Partial requires the stated limitation.
conventions.uq: Image UQ includes deterministic sets and posterior variability; it does not imply calibrated probabilities. Operator UQ requires uncertainty for operator parameters, not image variance caused by uncertain physics.
conventions.access: Full texts inspected online. No downloaded paper copies are added to the repository.
conventions.c1: All reviewed reports are primary research dated inside the existing search window; see version and canonical seed metadata.
conventions.c5: Every assessed record had an accessible English full text at source_url.
conventions.provenance: No reproducible database search or undocumented discovery date is inferred from this targeted batch.

records.title: AverNet: All-in-One Video Restoration for Time-Varying Unknown Degradations
records.technical: Alignment/enhancement prompts handle randomly combined, reordered and temporally varying synthetic degradations. DAVIS and Set8 tests vary degradation combinations and temporal intervals. Appendix A.4 acknowledges the need for real deployment validation. Prompts are not an explicit physical-operator estimate or posterior. Held-out intervals do not establish unseen-codec-family robustness.
records.applicability: Required compound-video baseline; P053 lineage remains unresolved.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Unsupervised Detection of Distribution Shift in Inverse Problems Using Diffusion Models
records.read_extent: §§2–4, Assumptions 1–2, Theorem 1 and Tables 1–2; appendix proofs not audited.
records.technical: Uses two pretrained scores to estimate dataset-level distribution shift from corrupted measurements. Its known linear operators satisfy structural assumptions, including a common right-singular basis and aggregate signal-space coverage. Inpainting and simulated MRI examples assess prior/content shift. This does not establish pointwise reconstruction coverage or uncertainty about an unknown operator.
records.applicability: Compare prior shift separately from acquisition mismatch.

4.evidence: Score-based estimator and cross-distribution imaging experiments; §§3–4.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

quality_followups: Independently audit theorem assumptions before reusing the KL identity.

records.title: Towards Distribution-Shift Uncertainty Estimation for Inverse Problems with Generative Priors
records.version: arXiv v1, 13 October 2025; final CAMSAP text not compared
records.technical: A learned proximal network trained on digit zero is tested on other MNIST digits with a known CT operator. Reconstruction variance tracks error under repeated noisy measurement simulations. Although the motivation discusses measurement subsets, the experiment uses independent measurement seeds. Variance is heuristic: no interval calibration or implemented abstention threshold is demonstrated. Null-space novelty can remain undetected.
records.applicability: Low-cost variance comparator; distinguish repeat acquisition from single-scan resampling.

1.evidence: arXiv v1, 13 October 2025; final CAMSAP text not compared

4.evidence: Learned proximal reconstruction, digit shifts and measurement repetitions; §IV.

records.title: InverseNet: Benchmarking Operator Mismatch and Calibration Across Compressive Imaging Modalities
records.technical: CACTI blind search estimates two of eight parameters, with six fixed to truth. Real captures test classical/PnP methods; deep-network hardware evaluation is deferred. Physical calibration is parameter fitting, not coverage.
records.applicability: Useful mismatch protocol; blind-parameter coverage is limited.

3.evidence: Controlled acquisition mismatch and blind calibration; §4.

4.evidence: Benchmark protocol, multiple solvers and hardware captures; §§3–4.

quality_followups: Reconcile Tables 1–2 against §4.4 before numerical synthesis.

records.title: On Hallucinations in Inverse Problems: Fundamental Limits and Provable Assessment Methods
records.read_extent: §§3.2–3.3, §4, §§5.3.3–5.4.1 and §§6–7; not every proof or experiment.
records.technical: Assessment uses a known forward map, a noise set and assumptions about realistic images. Remark 3.4 and Algorithm 2 approximate feasible-set diameter from below; this is not an upper certificate for pointwise reconstruction error. Detail-replacement tests use a known linear operator and constructed alternatives. MRI and paired super-resolution examples assess unsupported detail; feasibility searches can be inconclusive.
records.applicability: Sample disagreement alone cannot be treated as an upper error bound.

4.evidence: Theoretical assessment methods and imaging tests; §§3–5.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Adaptive Blind All-in-One Image Restoration
records.version: arXiv v1, 27 November 2024; CVIU 2026 version not compared
records.read_extent: §§3–5, Tables 1–6 and opening of Appendix B; code not audited.
records.technical: ABAIR combines synthetic pretraining, task adapters and predicted blending weights. Table 4 separates zero-shot tasks from newly trained adapters. Table 5 explicitly tests blur/noise, blur/JPEG and haze/snow combinations. Real low-light validation and cross-dataset tests are included. Degradation-class blending weights do not constitute a physical-operator posterior or calibrated uncertainty.
records.applicability: Strong discriminative comparator; match zero-shot versus adapted training budgets.

3.evidence: Unseen tasks and compound degradation; Tables 4–5.

records.title: Block Coordinate Plug-and-Play Methods for Blind Inverse Problems
records.read_extent: §§3–5.2 and §6; theorem statements and selected assumptions, not appendix proof verification.
records.technical: Block-coordinate PnP applies learned denoisers to image and operator-parameter blocks. Convergence statements depend on approximate-MMSE denoiser conditions and error bounds. Tests use retrospectively undersampled fastMRI and synthetic Gaussian deblurring. Joint inference is point estimation; random block updates and physical calibration are not posterior uncertainty or statistical coverage.
records.applicability: Existing joint-inference baseline with conditional convergence theory.

4.evidence: BC-PnP algorithm, conditional theory and imaging experiments; §§3–5.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Solving Inverse Problems with Model Mismatch using Untrained Neural Networks within Model-based Architectures
records.version: arXiv v1, 7 March 2024; final OpenReview version not compared
records.read_extent: Main §§3–6 and Proposition 4.1; no independent proof/code validation.
records.technical: An instance-adapted residual network corrects nominal forward predictions alongside reconstruction. Residual regularization assumes a useful nominal operator. Experiments include blur-parameter errors, synthetic seismic inversion and depth-based defogging. Random-initialization and iteration robustness are distinct from wrong-family guarantees. Proposition 4.1 relies on idealized convex-regularizer updates; objective descent alone is not general learned-network recovery.
records.applicability: Learned residual correction is already occupied; compare out-of-family acquisition explicitly.

1.evidence: arXiv v1, 7 March 2024; final OpenReview version not compared

4.evidence: A-adaptive unrolling/equilibrium networks and mismatch experiments; §§4–5.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: How to Trust Your Diffusion Model: A Convex Optimization Approach to Conformal Risk Control
records.read_extent: §§3.1–3.2, Algorithm 1, §§4–5 and Appendix D.3.2; proofs not audited.
records.technical: K-RCPS separates calibration-set optimization from risk-bound calibration. It controls average pixel miscoverage under the stated independent, identically distributed setup. Coverage of a generated posterior sample is explicitly distinguished from ground-truth-image coverage. Denoising experiments use known Gaussian noise on face and CT images. Neither arbitrary distribution shift nor selectively retained-region coverage follows automatically.
records.applicability: Baseline for risk control; specify the covered object and aggregation level.

4.evidence: Optimized prediction intervals and empirical coverage/width tests; §§3–4.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Task-Driven Uncertainty Quantification in Inverse Problems via Conformal Prediction
records.version: arXiv v1, 28 May 2024; final ECCV text not compared
records.technical: Conformal intervals target a classifier score on the true image, not necessarily the true clinical label. Conditional-flow samples support task-specific intervals under exchangeability. Retrospective fastMRI experiments include interval-width stopping for further acquisition. Single-round splits are slice-level; the multi-round experiment separates volumes. Marginal fixed-round coverage does not automatically establish coverage after adaptive stopping.
records.applicability: Acquisition deferral precedes us; audit dependence and stopping guarantees.

1.evidence: arXiv v1, 28 May 2024; final ECCV text not compared

3.evidence: Conformal task uncertainty and acquisition stopping; §§3–4.

4.evidence: Score intervals and retrospective MRI measurements; §5.

5.evidence: English full text accessed online at source_url.

records.title: Conformalized Generative Bayesian Imaging: An Uncertainty Quantification Framework for Computational Imaging
records.version: arXiv v1, 10 April 2025; final TCI text not compared
records.read_extent: §§II-A/B/E, III-A–G and IV–V; selected II-C/D, not every proof.
records.technical: Conditional generators combine image aleatoric uncertainty and neural-weight epistemic uncertainty with conformal likelihood-level sets. These are not operator-parameter posteriors. Experiments use simulated CT/MRI/inpainting measurements. MNIST coverage tests are separate from qualitative metal-implant and MRI-spike uncertainty examples; the latter do not establish calibrated OOD coverage.
records.applicability: Joint aleatoric/epistemic conformal imaging is existing work.

1.evidence: arXiv v1, 10 April 2025; final TCI text not compared

4.evidence: Conditional generators, intervals/sets and imaging experiments; §§II–III.

records.title: QUTCC: Quantile Uncertainty Training and Conformal Calibration for Imaging Inverse Problems
records.read_extent: §§3–6; Appendices A.1.1/A.1.2/A.3.2/A.4.1; no independent guarantee proof.
records.technical: Quantile-conditioned reconstruction calibrates lower and upper bounds and tests empirical coverage, including real fluorescence data. Appendix A.4.1 reports risk-stratified bins above target despite aggregate control. No operator posterior or explicit output rejection is demonstrated. Distribution shift remains future work.
records.applicability: Evaluate retained-region risk separately from average coverage.

4.evidence: Task-specific networks, coverage tests and FMD measurements; §4/Appendix A.
